facts.statement: Macelognathus was reclassified as a dinosaur by Moodie in 1908 and later identified as a crocodilian relative by Ostrom in 1971.
facts.quote: After being referred to the Dinosauria by Moodie in 1908, it was later reclassified by Ostrom in 1971 as a crocodilian relative.

facts.statement: In 2005, Göhlich and colleagues identified Macelognathus as a basal crocodylomorph known as a sphenosuchian based on new material from Fruita, Colorado.
facts.quote: Based on new material from the Morrison Formation at Fruita, Colorado, in 2005 Göhlich et al. identified it as a basal crocodylomorph ("sphenosuchian").

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Macelognathus might be a junior synonym of Hallopus victor because their specimens cannot be anatomically distinguished except for the larger size of the Macelognathus holotype.
facts.quote: It is possibly a junior synonym of Hallopus victor, since the known specimens of both taxa cannot currently be anatomically distinguished from each other, other than the much larger size of the holotype individual of Macelognathus.

facts.statement: Macelognathus possessed leaf-shaped, lanceolate teeth that lacked serrations.
facts.quote: Its teeth were leaf-shaped, lanceolate, and unserrated.

facts.statement: Due to a lack of bone evidence, Macelognathus likely did not have a horny covering on its lower jaw.
facts.quote: Due to a lack of osteological correlates for it, Macelognathus likely didn't have a horny covering (keratinous beak) on its lower jaw.

facts.statement: Macelognathus was an extinct genus of sphenosuchian crocodylomorph that lived during the Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: Macelognathus is an extinct genus of sphenosuchian crocodylomorph from the Late Jurassic.

facts.statement: Macelognathus lived in what is now Wyoming, North America.
facts.quote: It lived in what is now Wyoming, in North America.

facts.statement: Macelognathus measured between 1.2 and 1.9 meters in length.
facts.quote: Medía entre 1.2 y 1.9 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Macelognathus lived from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian stages, approximately 154.8 to 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (154.8 to 143.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: Macelognathus is classified within the family Hallopodidae.
Macelognathus is considered an example of convergent evolution because it shares similarities with caenagnathid dinosaurs despite not being closely related to them.
facts.quote: It is considered an example of convergent evolution, due to the similarities to caenagnathid dinosaurs, with which it was not closely related.

rejected.statement: The type species Macelognathus vagans was originally described by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1884 as a turtle based on a partial jaw found at Como Bluff, Wyoming.
rejected.quote: The type species, Macelognathus vagans, was described by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1884 as a turtle based on a partial jaw from the Late Jurassic Morrison Formation at Como Bluff, Wyoming.
